title: Local work tracker — Carina and the WorkTracker substrate — plan 001
epic_title: Local work tracker — Carina and the WorkTracker substrate

tasks.title: Establish the work-item core: model, store, create and show
tasks.goal: A work item is creatable and readable end to end — typed model, one-file-per-item store with atomic writes and exclusive-create identifiers, the Carina binary's first verbs, and the conformance-kit harness that every later behavior extends.
tasks.current: No work-item medium exists in this repo; the factory's only tracker is the hosted one, and the engine has no WorkTracker port to consume.
tasks.desired: Creating a work item persists one human-readable file under the configured work-items root and returns a stable sequential identifier that is never reused; showing it returns every field. The closed header grammar rejects an unknown key or out-of-set value with a defect naming file, operation, reason, and remedy, quarantining only that item. A simulated crash between the temporary write and the rename leaves the prior file intact. The work-items path key joins the closed config surface with its default at the operand root.
scope: the typed work-item model and the closed on-disk grammar (header, body, empty append log)
exclusive-create identifier allocation and the atomic write discipline
the WorkTracker port's first methods with the Carina create and show verbs over one core
the conformance-kit harness (a behavior table importing no adapter symbol) with its first rows
out_of_scope: transitions, comments, signals, hierarchy, dependencies, queries (later tasks)
any index, cache, daemon, or network surface
acceptance: create then show round-trips every header field and the body, in human and machine output, and the machine output validates against its golden schema
two hundred sequential creates yield two hundred distinct, never-reused identifiers, each resolvable by show
a malformed hand-edited item yields a defect naming file, operation, reason, and remedy, and every other item stays readable
the kit's atomic-write row passes: a simulated crash before rename leaves the prior version whole
key_interfaces: `WorkItem` — the typed model (header fields, body, log) with its closed value sets
`WorkTracker` — the consumer-side port; create and get are its first methods
`Defect` — the shared failure quadruple, rendered by the Carina binary
the conformance-kit behavior table — the executable port contract

tasks.title: Lifecycle: edit and idempotent transitions
tasks.goal: A work item's title, body, and open-closed state change safely: edits touch only the named fields, and transitions converge under repeats and races.
tasks.current: Items can be created and shown but never changed; there is no lifecycle.
tasks.desired: Edit updates the named fields and the updated stamp, leaving everything else byte-identical. Close and reopen apply idempotently — repeating an already-applied transition succeeds as a recorded no-op, never an error — and the close reason accepts only its closed value set, rejecting anything else with a named defect.
scope: the edit verb over title and body
close and reopen transitions with the transition audit entry in the append log
closed-set validation for state and close reason
out_of_scope: the rich lifecycle (readiness, triage) — projected later via signals and predicates, never stored as state
acceptance: an edit changes exactly the named fields plus the updated stamp; a diff shows no other mutation
closing a closed item succeeds as a recorded no-op, and the transition log carries one entry per applied change
an out-of-set close reason is refused with a defect naming the value and the allowed set
key_interfaces: `WorkTracker` — gains edit and transition methods; the Carina edit, close, and reopen verbs
the transition log entry — the audit record appended per applied change

tasks.title: The append log: comments and latest-wins decision records
tasks.goal: Dialogue and frozen judgments accumulate on a work item without loss: comments append forever, and decision records resolve latest-wins per namespace.
tasks.current: The append log exists structurally but nothing writes to it.
tasks.desired: Comments append in time order and are never rewritten. Decision records are typed, schema-versioned entries under a closed namespace set; the latest record per namespace is authoritative; an identical repeat writes nothing. Concurrent appends to one item serialize so no entry is lost.
scope: the comment verb and the append-only comment discipline
the record verb: namespaced decision records with latest-wins reads and idempotent repeats
per-item write serialization across the read-modify-write
out_of_scope: the meaning of any disposition (triage semantics live in the predicates task)
acceptance: a burst of interleaved appends from two writers lands every entry in order with zero loss
the latest record per namespace is returned as authoritative and an identical repeat is a recorded no-op
an out-of-set namespace is refused with a defect naming the value
key_interfaces: the log entry record — comment, decision-record, and transition kinds
`WorkTracker` — gains comment, record, and latest-record reads

tasks.title: Signals: the governed vocabulary
tasks.goal: Typed control state rides on work items through a governed signal vocabulary — names with roles and presentation — added and removed idempotently.
tasks.current: Items carry no signals; there is no vocabulary and no routing or authorization surface.
tasks.desired: The canonical seed vocabulary ships as a governed input under the store root: each signal has a name, a role from the closed role set, and presentation. Adding or removing a signal on an item is idempotent; adding an undefined signal is a defect naming it; operands may extend only the classification axis, never redefine engine-recognized names.
scope: the store-level signal vocabulary with the canonical seed set
signal add, remove, and define verbs with idempotent semantics
closed-role validation and the classification-only extension rule
out_of_scope: role-based selection (the query task) and readiness semantics (the predicates task)
acceptance: the seed vocabulary round-trips through the store and every signal reports its role
adding a present signal and removing an absent one both succeed as recorded no-ops
an undefined signal and an engine-recognized redefinition are each refused with a defect naming the offense
key_interfaces: the signal definition — name, role, presentation — and its vocabulary store
`WorkTracker` — gains signal mutation and vocabulary reads
tasks.overlap_accepted: parallel branch over shared packages; each verb self-registers from its own file into a derived command registry and each kit row into a self-registering conformance suite, and the WorkTracker port grows by per-concern sub-interfaces composed by embedding — extension is by new file, not shared-line append (AP-27, sharpening AP-23); the lone shared embed line falls to the recovery loop

tasks.title: Hierarchy: parents, children, and the epic rollup
tasks.goal: Work items form the Feature to Milestone to Epic to Task shape: parent links resolve both directions and an epic reports its open children exactly.
tasks.current: Items are flat; no parent relation or rollup exists.
tasks.desired: Setting or clearing a parent maintains the relation both directions. An epic reports the count and identity of its open children. The hierarchy-role value set is closed, and a parent reference to a nonexistent item is refused naming the target.
scope: parent set and clear with bidirectional resolution
the epic rollup read (open-children count and identities)
closed hierarchy-role validation
out_of_scope: dependency ordering (its own task) and any auto-close sweep (engine-era behavior)
acceptance: a child appears under its parent and the parent from the child, after set and after clear
an epic with a known fixture of children reports exactly its open ones
a parent reference to a missing item is refused with a defect naming the target
key_interfaces: `WorkTracker` — gains parent mutation and children reads; the Carina parent verbs
the hierarchy-role value set on the model

tasks.title: Dependencies: blocked-by edges with cycle refusal
tasks.goal: Ordering constraints are first-class edges: blocked-by relations resolve both directions, stay acyclic by refusal, and carry the cross-repo reference form opaquely.
tasks.current: No dependency relation exists; nothing can express ordering.
tasks.desired: Adding or removing a blocked-by edge maintains both directions. An edge that would close a cycle is refused with the cycle path named. A dangling target is refused naming it. The cross-repo reference form is stored and displayed without resolution.
scope: dependency add and remove with bidirectional resolution
the pre-write cycle check with the named-cycle refusal
opaque storage of the cross-repo reference form
out_of_scope: cross-repo resolution (deferred by the governing contract's waiting room)
acceptance: blockers and blocking both resolve after add and after remove
an edge closing a cycle is refused with the full cycle path named and the edge set unchanged
a dangling target and a malformed reference are each refused with a defect naming them
key_interfaces: `WorkTracker` — gains dependency mutation and edge reads; the Carina dep verbs

tasks.title: Queries: list, filter, and exact search
tasks.goal: The backlog is discoverable: list with state and signal filters returns bounded, stably-ordered sets, and text search matches exactly — never fuzzily.
tasks.current: Items can only be read one by one; no listing, filtering, or search exists.
tasks.desired: List filters by state and by signal name or role, returning a deterministic creation-ordered set — including selecting the factory-implementable set by its authorization-role signal. Search over titles, bodies, and comments returns every exact match and only exact matches. Every query emits schema-versioned machine output beside the human form.
scope: list with state and signal (name and role) filters, stable-sorted
exact substring and token search over titles, bodies, and comments
golden-schema machine output for both verbs
out_of_scope: any search index (direct scan; an index is a measured-need decision recorded in the design's open questions)
acceptance: a fixture corpus returns the exact expected set and order for each filter, including the authorization-role selection
a near-miss token does not match and the fixture yields zero false positives
both verbs' machine output validates against golden schemas
key_interfaces: the query parameters type — state, signal, role, text
`WorkTracker` — gains list and search; the Carina list and search verbs

tasks.title: The shared predicates: ready-set and triage-set
tasks.goal: The engine's dispatch questions get one answer each: the ready-set and triage-set predicates exist exactly once, shared verbatim by the port and the Carina verbs.
tasks.current: Readiness and undecidedness are not computable; no predicate exists anywhere.
tasks.desired: The ready-set predicate — open, carrying the authorization signal, no open blocker, not a structural rollup, no closing disposition — and the triage-set predicate — open, no triage decision record, not a structural rollup, no open blocker, not in flight — each have exactly one implementation. The port and the CLI return byte-identical sets over any corpus, and destructive-decision reads reflect every prior write with no cache in the path.
scope: the two predicate implementations over the model, consumed by port and CLI alike
the ready and triage verbs
direct-read discipline on the decision path
out_of_scope: fairness, rotation, or scheduling order (engine-era; the predicate only answers membership)
acceptance: the ready set over a fixture corpus matches the hand-computed expectation exactly
the triage set over the same corpus matches its hand-computed expectation exactly
the CLI and the port return byte-identical sets for both predicates
a membership read immediately after a qualifying write reflects that write
key_interfaces: the ready and triage predicate functions — the single shared implementations
`WorkTracker` — gains the two set reads; the Carina ready and triage verbs

tasks.title: The fault suites: strong reads, crash safety, and contention
tasks.goal: The store's integrity claims become executable evidence: interleave, crash-injection, parallel-create, and concurrent-append suites join the conformance kit and run in the race-enabled build.
tasks.current: Atomicity and identifier discipline exist as implementation behavior with unit coverage, but no adversarial suite proves them under interleaving, crashes, or process concurrency.
tasks.desired: An interleave suite shows every post-write read on a decision path reflecting the write. A crash-injection suite across the write sequence's cut points yields zero torn or lost state. A multi-process parallel-create stress yields zero identifier collision or reuse. A concurrent-append stress loses zero log entries. All four ride the conformance kit.
scope: the interleave (read-your-writes) suite
crash injection across the atomic-write cut points
parallel-create and concurrent-append stress harnesses
out_of_scope: networked-filesystem semantics (out of the governing contract's scope)
acceptance: the interleave suite reports read-your-writes in every case
crash injection at each cut point leaves items wholly old or wholly new with zero losses
a multi-process create stress completes with zero collision and zero reuse
a two-writer append stress completes with zero lost entries
key_interfaces: the conformance-kit fault rows — the executable form of the store's integrity invariants

tasks.title: Prove the medium: hermetic lifecycle, capacity, and survival
tasks.goal: The finished medium is proven as a whole: a full lifecycle runs hermetically, queries hold their latency bounds at the capacity target, and the backlog survives factory removal.
tasks.current: Individual behaviors pass their suites, but no end-to-end, capacity, or survival evidence exists.
tasks.desired: A complete lifecycle — create, signal, link, comment, record, transition, query, close — completes with zero network syscalls. List, search, ready, and triage meet the governing contract's latency bounds on a ten-thousand-item fixture. Deleting the factory footprint leaves the store intact and readable. Every defect across a fixture sweep names its full quadruple.
scope: the hermetic end-to-end lifecycle check with a syscall trace
the capacity fixture and timed query suite
the survival check and the defect-quadruple sweep
out_of_scope: performance tuning beyond meeting the stated bounds (an index remains a measured-need decision)
acceptance: the full lifecycle completes with zero network syscalls in the trace
list, search, ready, and triage meet the stated latency bounds on the ten-thousand-item fixture
deleting the factory footprint leaves every work item readable and the kit green
a defect sweep shows file, operation, reason, and remedy on every failure case
key_interfaces: the hermetic end-to-end harness and the capacity fixture — the medium's proof surface
